column2: Switch OFF and take both cells out while assembling. If the chassis top plate is already fitted, take it off first: level-1 items are mounted while the top plate is still open.

Left and right in this part are seen from behind the robot, facing forward. Put every item in its place following the layout drawing, without bolts and without ties: level 1 on the bottom plate, level 2 on the top plate, level 3 on the third plate (the top plate and third plate are laid side by side on the table).

Level 1 (bottom plate): four motors on the left and right sides, the motor cans facing the center. LM2596 #1 and #2 lie one after another along the center line. #1 at the back with OUT facing back; #2 is rotated 180° from the dry-stack photo so its IN faces the back and its OUT the front. Front end: MPU6050 flat (writing facing forward), the TB6612 in front of it, WAGO 6V on the left and WAGO −6 on the right. Rear end: the rear HC-SR04 facing backward, WAGO + on the left and WAGO − on the right.

Level 2 (top plate): holder 1 at the very back with the spring (−) on the left, holder 2 in front of it flipped (spring on the right), the BMS in front of it (8.4V and 0V pads on the left), the switch in front of the BMS on the right, the fuse in front of the switch, breadboard 1 across the middle, the DevKit on the 30P board at front left, the XL4015 at front right rotated 180° from the photo so the IN terminal (the 100 µF 50 V capacitor side) faces back, the front HC-SR04 at the front edge, straight ahead.

Height check: temporarily fit the top plate on the kit standoffs, place the level-2 items, stack two brass standoffs on each leg, put the third plate on top. Look from the side: nothing touches the plate above it, and the battery cells can be pulled out of the holders without opening level 3.
Wire check: lay out every wire cut in Parts 1-4 along its route. All must reach without tension. If any is short, extend it now, before the plate is closed.
Photograph from above and from the side, then lift off the third plate and the top plate again.
The top plate is still off, the switch OFF, the cells out of the holders.

How to fit nylon standoffs: the standoff's thread goes through the plate hole from above, the nut under the plate; the module sits on top of the standoff, locked with an M3x6 bolt. LM2596 #1 and #2 on the center line with 6 mm standoffs (M3*6+6) in their corner holes (#2 already rotated 180°). The MPU6050 with 6 mm standoffs, flat, writing facing forward.

Modules without holes are held with cable ties: the TB6612, all four WAGOs (levers facing up so they can still be opened), and the rear HC-SR04 (two ties on the outer side of the sensor cylinders, tilted up about 5° so it does not read the floor). Pass the tie through two holes or gaps in the plate on either side of the module, loop it over the module, lock it under the plate. Tighten until it does not wobble, no more, then cut the tail flush.
If no hole fits: stick masking tape on the drilling spot, drill slowly with a 3 mm bit without pressing, no closer than 5 mm to the edge, because acrylic cracks easily.

Level-1 connections: motor wires to AO1/AO2 and BO1/BO2 of the TB6612, green-black from WAGO 6V/−6 to VM/GND of the TB6612 and the 470 µF capacitor on WAGO 6V/−6 (Part 2), the WAGO +/− wires to the IN of both LM2596 (Part 1).

Signal wires that go up: 9 F-F wires from the TB6612 (to the 30P board, 20 cm is enough), 4 F-F wires from the MPU6050 (to the I2C header of the 30P board, 18 cm (no. 31)), 4 wires from the rear HC-SR04 (to breadboard 1, 18 cm (no. 30)).
The XL4015 wires (red-black from WAGO +/−, green-black to WAGO 6V/−6) are also left reaching upward.
Gather the power wires that go up at the big central hole in the top plate, and the signal wires at the gap near the TB6612. Tie each group loosely so they do not touch the wheels.

The holders, BMS, switch and fuse have been connected to WAGO +/− on level 1 since Part 1. Lift that battery circuit up onto the top plate, then lower the plate slowly while feeding all the wires that go up through its holes and gaps. Make sure no wire is pinched between the plate and the standoffs.

Level-3 legs: each bolt holding the top plate to a kit standoff is replaced by a brass standoff: its male thread goes through the top plate hole into the kit standoff. Stack one more standoff, making each leg 60 mm. Fit at all six points: 4 corners and 2 on the middle wings, so the level-3 plate does not flex when the STOP button or display is pressed.

18650 holders: a short M3 bolt from inside the holder through the center hole of its base, the nut under the plate (holder 2 flipped). Do not use a cable tie across the top of a holder, because the cell then cannot be pulled out.

The BMS, switch and fuse are held with cable ties. Breadboard 1 is moved together with the wires already plugged in from Part 2, then held with two cable ties across both its ends (over the empty rails). The 30P board and XL4015 (already rotated 180°) on 8 mm nylon standoffs (M3*8+6). The DevKit with upright wires comes to about 53 mm, still under the level-3 plate (60 mm). The front HC-SR04 stands at the front edge with two ties, straight ahead, about 6 cm above the floor.
Connect the power wires that go up: red-black from WAGO +/− to IN+/IN− of the XL4015, green-black from WAGO 6V/−6 to OUT+/OUT− of the XL4015. Tighten the screw terminals.
The black GND from LM2596 #1 to the GND pin of the 30P board's power block. Its red 5 V is not plugged in yet (that is Stage 6).
Signal wires: the TB6612 to S pins D25, D26, D27, D13, D32, D33 and STBY/VCC to 3V as in Part 2 Stage 3. The MPU6050 to the I2C header. The battery-gauge wire to a20.

The rear HC-SR04 (far from the 30P board, so through the breadboard): VCC → c30, GND → the blue line, ECHO → a12, TRIG → e18. A new 13 cm wire (no. 27) from a18 → S pin of row D14. The front HC-SR04 as in Part 2 Stage 5.

The wires that continue to level 3 are gathered at the front, near the front standoff leg: 5 V + GND for the S3 board, 5 V + GND for the camera, servo power, and the 3 UART wires (their female ends are plugged in now to D16, D17 and G of the 30P board).
Feed the wires up from level 2 through the third plate's holes, then fit the third plate on the legs with M3 bolts.

The orange wires of both servos go down to level 2 through M-F wires: pan → S pin D23, tilt → S pin D4. The STOP button wires go down to breadboard 1: one to d27, one to g29 (replacing the diagonal legs of the 6 mm button).
Switch OFF: turn the head by hand fully left and right, then nod. The camera and servo wires are not pulled, and the head does not touch the TFT.
Tie the wires in groups: power (red, green, black), motors, servos, signals. Keep power and motor wires away from the display's SPI wires and the microphone.
Label the ends of important wires that are not yet labeled: "5V S3", "5V CAM", "5V DEVKIT", "UART TX", "UART RX".
Tighten all the screw terminals once more. Insert both cells (cell 1 then cell 2).
Switch OFF, unplug all USB cables.

Plug in the red 5 V ends from LM2596 #1: one to the 5V pin of the 30P board's power block, one to the 5V pin of the S3 board's power block. The camera's 5 V wire from LM2596 #2 has been fitted since Part 4.
Move the MAX98357A Vin from the 3.3 V rail to the S3 board's 5V pin, so the speaker is louder and does not load the 3.3 V.
Check with continuity: all the GNDs (BMS P−, the three converters, both expansion boards, the ESP32-CAM, the TB6612) beep to each other.
Switch ON. Within 10 seconds: the DevKit's blue LED lights, the face appears on the display, the speaker greets you, the Telegram bot sends a message.
Measure LM2596 #1 OUT once more with everything on: still above 4.9 V.

If you postponed the Part 2 Stage 8 safety tests, run them now with the robot lifted (wheels touching nothing): refuse forward when there is an obstacle, the STOP button latches, and the wheels stop by themselves after 3 seconds. Only then move to the floor.
Put the robot on the floor, away from stairs and fragile things. Hand near the STOP button.
Send /status. Check that the front and rear distances make sense.
Send /maju 500. The robot goes forward for half a second. If it veers by itself, one side is weaker; that is normal for cheap TT motors.
Send /kiri then /kanan: the robot spins on the spot.
Put a 30 cm box in front of the robot, send /maju 3000. The robot must stop before about 20 cm.
Press the STOP button while the robot moves: it stops at once, Telegram notifies you. Press again to release.
Try /ikuti then walk slowly in front of the robot. Try /jaga then walk past it after 4 seconds.
Speed: the number 150 in the forward command is 59% power. If it is too fast for your room, change the number in tanganiPesan and tanganiSentuh in the brain code.
Stop distance: JARAK_STOP_DEPAN in the body code. A slippery floor needs a larger distance because the robot slides.
Head: TILT_MIN, TILT_MAX in the body code. Pan direction in the AI: if "lihat ke kiri" turns right instead, change the note "pan 30=kanan 150=kiri" in promptSistem.
Battery: repeat the BATERAI_FAKTOR calibration with the multimeter if the number is off.
Upside-down camera: KAMERA_TERBALIK in the eye code. The robot's personality: change the sentences in promptSistem.
